findings.page_quote: Analysis population intention-to-treat; older-adult evidence includes one whole trial and one pre-specified JUPITER >=70-years subgroup

source_evidence.quote: Effect estimates from this exploratory analysis with age cut-point chosen after trial completion should be viewed in the context of the overall trial results.

findings.claim: The JUPITER age subgroup is incorrectly described as pre-specified. The source explicitly states that the age cut-point was chosen after trial completion.

source_evidence.quote: Serious adverse events occurred in 131 participants (2.7%) in the atorvastatin group and in 129 (2.7%) in the placebo group, with musculoskeletal, hepatobiliary, and diabetes-related adverse events occurring more commonly in the atorvastatin group.

findings.claim: The reason-code audit incorrectly labels the refusal as false because an outcome-specific value is held; the same error appears for new-onset diabetes. The quoted numbers describe aggregate serious adverse events, while neither registered harm has specific counts or an effect with CI in this abstract.

screening.reason: This is an older-adult analysis of randomized rosuvastatin versus placebo in participants without cardiovascular disease. The exploratory age cut does not remove the randomized treatment comparison.
screening.quote: INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive 20 mg of rosuvastatin daily or placebo.

screening.reason: The abstract directly establishes the eligible age, primary-prevention population, randomized statin intervention, and placebo comparator.
screening.quote: Community-dwelling adults at least 70 years of age with no history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or dementia were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive atorvastatin at a dose of 40 mg once daily or identical placebo.
